title: Trial of Toil
function: Bjorn must discover whether he still has something useful to offer when the household no longer needs him to command it.
sourceAuthority: current user direction: Astrid remains largely outside foreground action in Issues 6–7
dramaticRule: The support group changes Bjorn's behavior; it does not replace the rest of his life. Ordinary life tests the distinction between command, responsibility, intervention, participation and trust through a small number of harder situations rather than a chain of repetitive requested-help demonstrations.
astridContinuity: Astrid is one of exactly three Kin and is largely absent from foreground action in this issue. Her absence is ordinary rather than mysterious: she is simply out living a part of her day the others are not following. Do not explain or inventory that life yet. The two male Kin remain visible household presences; do not create replacement Kin.

bjornArc.setup: Issue 5 proves that the household and neighborhood can function without Bjorn managing every need. What should feel like success instead threatens the provider identity on which his authority was built.
bjornArc.rupture: After a minor electrical hazard is already contained, Bjorn vents his uselessness by smashing the dead power strip into the wall. Carrie treats the frightening behavior as a real problem, not a cultural joke.
bjornArc.catalyst: Carrie offers a DTI temporal-refugee support group because the people there know what it is to lose a role, sequence, and expected future.
bjornArc.change: Bjorn learns a difficult distinction: seeing what someone needs does not entitle him to decide for them. He begins asking whether people want counsel, help, or simply a witness.
bjornArc.proof: The issue tests the change through distinct categories rather than repetition: requested judgment, immediate safety without prior permission, shared household obligation, belonging without debt, emotional witnessing, tolerating independent household lives, trusted responsibility, and finally offering help without seizing another person's task.
bjornArc.result: Bjorn finishes the issue with meaningful work but no new office, title, or command. People value his judgment because it is available rather than imposed.

pageSpine.title: Known Here
pageSpine.entry: Morning in the Safe Cave. Gunnar and the two male Kin are already handling breakfast, bags, laundry and small household tasks. Astrid is already out.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn reaches for several jobs and finds none require him.
pageSpine.exit: A functioning household feels uncomfortably like a household that has outgrown its leader.

pageSpine.title: No Debt
pageSpine.entry: At the bodega, Bjorn tries to repay accumulated small kindnesses with disproportionate labor.
pageSpine.turn: The Bodega Owner refuses to turn friendship into a debt ledger and tells him to stop moving a delivery that belongs to a paid worker.
pageSpine.exit: Being known does not automatically give Bjorn a job.

pageSpine.title: Provision
pageSpine.entry: Back home, Carrie finds Bjorn increasingly irritable while everyone else continues with the day.
pageSpine.turn: He names the actual wound: food, law, roads, money and household survival are now carried by systems and other people.
pageSpine.exit: Carrie understands that gratitude is not the problem; usefulness is.

pageSpine.title: The Rupture
pageSpine.entry: A cheap power strip sparks. Gunnar unplugs it and one of the male Kin moves the nearby bedding before there is real danger.
pageSpine.turn: After the problem is over, Bjorn smashes the dead strip into the wall because he had nothing to save.
pageSpine.exit: The room goes quiet. Carrie tells him that frightening his own household is not protection.

pageSpine.title: A Choice
pageSpine.entry: Carrie tells Bjorn about a temporal-refugee group without presenting it as punishment, treatment compliance or a condition of housing.
pageSpine.turn: She says only that the people there have also lost the lives in which they knew what they were for.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn chooses to go.

pageSpine.title: Not Ancient
pageSpine.entry: First group meeting. Bjorn initially sorts people by how long ago they came from.
pageSpine.turn: A participant from 1987 rejects being treated as ancient and describes returning to a world where parents are dead and a younger sibling is old.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn stops measuring displacement in centuries.

pageSpine.title: A Council Without Orders
pageSpine.entry: Bjorn expects the room to have a person who decides what must be said.
pageSpine.turn: The group leader establishes that anyone may speak, pass, disagree or leave a question unanswered.
pageSpine.exit: The boundary interests Bjorn because it is firm without being hierarchical.

pageSpine.title: Truth Is Not Owed
pageSpine.entry: Bjorn hears a participant describe being fine while plainly describing a life in collapse.
pageSpine.turn: He presses the contradiction too hard. The leader stops him: noticing truth is not ownership of another person's disclosure.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn leaves angry because the correction makes sense.

pageSpine.title: Worth the Argument
pageSpine.entry: Carrie waits outside after the meeting.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn emerges still arguing with the leader rather than dismissing the group.
pageSpine.exit: Carrie realizes he has found an adult relationship in which disagreement itself feels respectful.

pageSpine.title: Decision or Judgment
pageSpine.entry: At the apartment, the two male Kin disagree over a shared household object while Gunnar refuses to referee.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn begins to issue a ruling, catches himself, and asks whether they want a decision or his judgment.
pageSpine.exit: They want his judgment. Authority becomes requested.

pageSpine.title: Before Permission
pageSpine.entry: On the fifth-floor stairs, the Upstairs Neighbor loses her footing while carrying laundry.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn catches her immediately without waiting to be asked, then starts to take the basket and is stopped.
pageSpine.exit: He learns that urgent safety can justify immediate action without turning the rest of another person's task into his.

pageSpine.title: Not a Rule
pageSpine.entry: Gunnar and the two male Kin return with groceries while Bjorn deliberately waits to be invited before touching anything.
pageSpine.turn: Gunnar points out that nobody had to ask him either; carrying one's share of household work is participation, not commandeering.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn sees that he has turned waiting into another rigid rule and corrects back toward ordinary shared responsibility.

pageSpine.title: Nothing Today
pageSpine.entry: At the bodega, Bjorn automatically scans for a debt to repay or labor that needs doing.
pageSpine.turn: The Bodega Owner gives him his usual coffee and tells him there is nothing to fix or carry today.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn remains anyway. Ordinary familiarity is allowed to matter without being converted into labor.

pageSpine.title: He Knows the Way
pageSpine.entry: Carrie arrives expecting to escort Bjorn to the next group session.
pageSpine.turn: Gunnar tells her Bjorn already left; Gunnar showed him the route once and Bjorn chose to return independently.
pageSpine.exit: The group is Bjorn's relationship now, not Carrie's program.

pageSpine.title: What Do You Want?
pageSpine.entry: At the next support-group meeting, the 1987 Participant asks about a family dinner that keeps turning them into a period exhibit.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn stops before deciding for them, asks what they actually want, and offers a stated boundary plus an exit rather than a verdict.
pageSpine.exit: His judgment supplies structure without taking ownership of the decision.

pageSpine.title: No Clean Choice
pageSpine.entry: The 1987 Participant points out that leaving may hurt their brother while staying may turn them into entertainment.
pageSpine.turn: Asked which choice is right, Bjorn admits neither is cheap and that he cannot make the cost disappear.
pageSpine.exit: The participant makes their own decision; Bjorn learns that respecting agency does not guarantee a clean or painless outcome.

pageSpine.title: Work and Worth
pageSpine.entry: Afterward Bjorn argues with the leader that an adult needs work that matters.
pageSpine.turn: The leader agrees about meaningful contribution but rejects the idea that usefulness determines whether someone deserves care.
pageSpine.exit: Neither wins. Bjorn leaves with a distinction he cannot dismiss.

pageSpine.title: Counsel or Witness
pageSpine.entry: Back in the neighborhood, someone begins unloading a frustrating modern problem onto Bjorn.
pageSpine.turn: He asks whether they want counsel or witness. They choose witness.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn remains present without fixing anything.

pageSpine.title: Not Everything Comes Through Him
pageSpine.entry: The apartment is busy. Gunnar has books; the two male Kin have separate tasks; Astrid is again not in the foreground and nobody treats that as an emergency.
pageSpine.turn: Bjorn realizes he does not know where every member of the household is or what every person is doing.
pageSpine.exit: He allows that fact to remain true.

pageSpine.title: Watch the Counter
pageSpine.entry: At the bodega near closing, the owner has to go downstairs for two minutes and asks Bjorn to stay by the counter without touching the register.
pageSpine.turn: A familiar customer takes coffee, leaves exact cash, and goes; Bjorn observes rather than policing a relationship he does not own.
pageSpine.exit: The owner returns and makes clear that simply being trusted to be there was the work.

pageSpine.title: Something He Said
pageSpine.entry: The 1987 participant finds Bjorn outside the formal circle after the family gathering.
pageSpine.turn: They used his boundary, left when displayed, and were later invited back under better terms.
pageSpine.exit: His judgment changed something real without controlling the outcome.

pageSpine.title: The Thing He Would Not Name
pageSpine.entry: At a later group meeting Bjorn finally volunteers his own problem rather than analyzing someone else's.
pageSpine.turn: He admits that if nobody needs his protection, he does not know what his place is.
pageSpine.exit: The leader tells him a hand can be offered before it is required.

pageSpine.title: Offer, Don't Seize
pageSpine.entry: Back home, Bjorn sees several tasks in progress and offers one male Kin help without reaching for the tool.
pageSpine.turn: The offer is declined and Bjorn accepts the no, then starts the shared coffee routine on his own while Gunnar later asks for his judgment on a book illustration.
pageSpine.exit: Bjorn can now initiate shared work, offer help, accept refusal and contribute without making himself the organizing principle.

pageSpine.title: Work That Matters
pageSpine.entry: Evening. People return to separate routines; the household is busy without being organized around Bjorn.
pageSpine.turn: Carrie asks how the group is going. Bjorn looks at the apartment, where his presence matters but is not the organizing principle, and answers: 'There is work here.'
pageSpine.exit: He enters Issue 7 able to lead people whose choices remain their own.

issueBridge.issue6Question: Can Bjorn contribute without making himself indispensable?
issueBridge.towardIssue7: Bjorn can now gather people and take responsibility without assuming unity requires obedience or one answer.
issueBridge.towardIssue8: Astrid's increasingly independent life remains mostly outside Bjorn, Carrie and the reader's view, preserving the later courtroom reveal rather than explaining it in advance.

boundaries.clinicalRole: Bjorn remains a participant, not a therapist or clinician.
boundaries.groupDependence: The group functions without Bjorn and does not become his new command structure.
boundaries.groupScreenTime: The support group remains a catalyst and occupies only the pages needed for distinct dramatic turns. Do not add additional practice scenes merely to restate 'wait to be asked.'
boundaries.astrid: Astrid is largely absent from foreground action. Do not explain where she spends all of that time and do not imply danger, disappearance or estrangement.
boundaries.kinCount: Exactly three Kin exist: Astrid and two men. Do not add background Kin to make the apartment feel fuller.
boundaries.demotedMaterial: Do not restore the old Community College/DMV chain merely because it exists in archival source.
boundaries.practiceRepetition: Do not restore the removed sequence of flour-bag / stool / flat-pack / refrigerator / requested-hand demonstrations. The revised issue deliberately differentiates emergency action, shared obligations, ordinary belonging, trust and offered help.
